### Maturity resources and exclusions

Section 2.5 requires all then-outstanding senior loan principal at Termination Date; section 4.3 ends commitments at 5 p.m. New York time that day. Therefore the budget's unused availability1m cannot repay this same facility or be extended past termination. Pre-termination borrowing used to repay the same loan merely changes balances within the facility, not external takeout resources. Commitment reduction on rollup repayment and specified sweeps also prevents assuming all paydowns recycle (maturity-supplement pp.1–2).

The senior diagnostic includes cash loans and senior rollup **once**. Rollups repay prepetition RBL and are not a second operating inflow. Junior650m remains separate; it is neither deducted from senior availability nor included in the senior diagnostic. Terminal interest/fees, other claims, any reserve to keep the business operating and LC replacement/collateral remain outside the principal-only gap. Existing budget interest/fee uses are already in net cash flow; no full row is deducted again. Complete payoff sources/uses must reconcile any unpaid terminal accruals to what the budget already pays.

LC face amount is not automatically additive cash payable at maturity: establish actual outstanding amounts, drawings, collateral offsets, expiry/replacement and demands under sections 3.4/3.8. The L/C Maturity Date precedes stated maturity by five business days; a Majority Lenders request can require collateral then or at earlier termination, and outstanding uncollateralized maturity LCs can become Unpaid Drawings (filing-captures pp.3–4; maturity-supplement p.1).
